research_content_reliability.label: Research-content reliability
research_content_reliability.definition: Signals that the reliability, reproducibility, validity, or evidentiary integrity of the research content itself is questioned.
include: computer/AI-generated article content when it affects content authenticity
paper-mill or fabricated article production when it indicates article-level reliability risk
exclude: journal/publisher procedural acts without a content reliability signal
research_content_reliability.manuscript_link: Supports discussion of the reliability of the published product/scientific record, without assigning fault.

attribution_authorship_disclosure_integr.label: Attribution, authorship, and disclosure integrity
attribution_authorship_disclosure_integr.definition: Signals concerning who created, approved, owned, disclosed, cited, or was credited for the work, including attribution and disclosure problems.
exclude: generic data/image/results unreliability without attribution/authorship/disclosure element
attribution_authorship_disclosure_integr.manuscript_link: Matches the manuscript's concern with transparent relationships among authors, editors, reviewers, and publishers and with disclosure/attribution integrity.

editorial_peer_review_governance.label: Editorial and peer-review governance
editorial_peer_review_governance.definition: Signals that editorial decision-making, peer review, journal/publisher procedures, or editorial independence/governance mechanisms are implicated.
include: publication-policy breach or sanction when it concerns publication governance
exclude: journal/publisher investigation as source only unless the reason itself concerns editorial/peer-review procedure
content unreliability without editorial or peer-review process signal
editorial_peer_review_governance.manuscript_link: Directly supports the manuscript's themes of peer-review integrity, editorial independence, proportionality, and governance.

post_publication_transparency_due_proces.label: Post-publication transparency, due process, and oversight
post_publication_transparency_due_proces.definition: Signals concerning post-publication investigation, notice transparency, correction/retraction status, availability/removal, procedural communication, institutional/legal oversight, or appeal/objection-related process.
include: notice lacks information or is inaccessible
exclude: data/image/results problems without post-publication process information
peer-review compromise as pre-publication process unless linked to post-publication oversight
attribution/authorship issues without procedural transparency/oversight component
post_publication_transparency_due_proces.manuscript_link: Matches the manuscript's core language on transparency, clear reasons, proportionality, due process, appeal, and publisher/journal oversight.

guardrails: Retraction Watch Reason terms are curated, non-exclusive metadata signals, not adjudicated fault.
The four manuscript categories are secondary semantic aggregations created for figure readability, not original Retraction Watch fields.
A record can map to multiple categories; percentages are record-level prevalence and may sum above 100%.
Investigation-by-X remains a process/source signal, not fault by X.
